facts.text: Mayfair is an affluent area of Westminster in Central London and serves as the principal location for the series Bridgerton.
Mayfair became well known for an annual fair that took place from 1686 to 1764 in what is now Shepherd Market.
The Royal Academy of Arts in Mayfair was founded in 1768 by George III and is the oldest fine arts society in the world.
Savile Row in south-eastern Mayfair became a hub for tailors starting in 1803, attracted by the area's affluent residents.
Mayfair's prestigious status is commemorated by being the most expensive property square on the London Monopoly board.
The north-western part of Mayfair has subsequently been nicknamed Little Doha.
